clue.text: Artist from Lambeth possibly on benefits

indicators.note: in a clue, one thing placed 'on' another sits after it, so the second part is written after the first

parts.note: gains are benefits or advantages
Lambeth is a London borough; 'possibly' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A painter from south London is supposedly living on state handouts.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambeth is an inner London borough south of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was an eighteenth-century English portrait and landscape painter.

clue.text: After fault is raised, discard small gadget

indicators.note: the remaining parts are placed after the first one in sequence
in a down clue, raising something makes it read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a bug is a fault in a system or program
to bin something is to throw it away
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Once a defect has come to light, throw away the little device.
explanation.walkthrough: Gubbins is a British informal word for a gadget or for bits and pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gubbins is a British colloquial word for an unnamed device or piece of equipment, a thingummy.

clue.text: Head of practice denied operating illegally, becoming furious

indicators.note: what is denied is refused, so that letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: pirate as an adjective, as in pirate radio, describes an illegal operation

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the initial of practice, which is removed

explanation.surface: A senior partner refused permission to trade unlawfully loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a direct synonym for very angry or furious.

clue.text: Succeeded with lawsuit to secure new licence

indicators.note: with means alongside, so one part is set next to the other

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so this word is wrapped around a letter

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit brought in court
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A company won its court case to obtain a fresh permit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanction is an official permission or authorisation, the same as a licence to act.

clue.text: President of Vietnam about to be shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, showing something up means it reads from bottom to top
of here means made from, so the letters come straight out of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Vietnam and the start of about

explanation.surface: A head of state from Vietnam is about to be exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'about to be' as 'soon to be'; 'about' is only supplying letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama was the forty-fourth President of the United States.

clue.text: Whoever struggles gets blame regularly for defeat

indicators.note: something that struggles is twisting and thrashing about, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of blame

explanation.surface: Whoever is losing ends up taking the blame for the loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm an opponent is to defeat them completely, crushing them by force.

clue.text: Spin from vacuous guy introducing measure

indicators.note: one part introducing another comes first and leads into it
vacuous means empty, so the word loses its inside and only the outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of guy
a rate is a measure, as of speed or frequency

explanation.surface: An empty-headed bloke brings in a new way of spinning things.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to spin or whirl round in circles about a centre.

clue.text: Immature urge Dean disguised

indicators.note: something disguised has its appearance changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Dean hides a childish impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone underage is too young for something by law, hence not yet mature or adult.

clue.text: Originally stylish and elegant, old clothes deteriorate

indicators.note: to clothe something is to cover it, so this word goes round the other letters

parts.note: worn means old and much used

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the initials of stylish and elegant

explanation.surface: Once smart and graceful, aged garments go downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun after 'old'; it is a verb, meaning wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: To worsen is to become worse, which is what deteriorating means.

clue.text: Showing courage when tackling excellent opponents provides inspiration

indicators.note: tackling means grappling with, taking hold of, so the first word goes around the others

parts.note: brave means showing courage
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as the letter I
North and West are opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Being bold when taking on top rivals inspires the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The insert goes in after the second letter. In bridge North-South play East-West, so a pair like N and W are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever idea, a flash of inspiration.

clue.text: Capital's content to back run for musical composition

indicators.note: backing something means coming behind it, so this part follows the other
the content of something is what is inside, so its first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
London is the capital of the UK

explanation.surface: The city is content to bankroll a staging of a new piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy'; it means the inside, ONDO, of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a recurring theme alternates with contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Occasionally regrets ousting Democrat from country, finding apathy

indicators.note: ousting someone means pushing them out and taking their place
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of regrets
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
India is a country

explanation.surface: Sometimes sorry about expelling a politician from the nation, people grow indifferent.
explanation.walkthrough: ERT takes the place of the D in INDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a lack of energy or will to act, the sluggish indifference of apathy.

clue.text: Maybe area between Arab's shoulder blades becomes dry

definitions.text: Maybe area between Arab's shoulder blades
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades; an Arab is a breed of horse
second meaning: a verb for drying up and shrivelling

explanation.surface: A desert dweller's upper back dries out in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' looks like a person, but it is the horse breed; 'Maybe' marks it as one example of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The withers are the highest part of a horse's back; a plant that withers shrivels as it dries.

clue.text: Reportedly rowers representing county get breathless

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the answer sounds like the words described

parts.note: Suffolk is a county in eastern England
an eight is a racing boat crew of eight rowers

explanation.surface: Rowers racing for their county are said to run out of puff.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'Suffolk eight', a county's boat crew, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffocate is to be unable to breathe, an extreme way to be left breathless.

clue.text: Keen to follow motorsport thread

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this part is placed second

parts.note: Formula One, F1, with the 1 written as the letter I
to keen is to wail in grief, to lament

explanation.surface: An enthusiast keen to follow motor racing joins a discussion thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' is the verb meaning to wail, not the adjective meaning eager.
explanation.definitionFit: A filament is a fine thread or fibre, such as the wire in a light bulb.

clue.text: Vegetable lorry that man Roger stops

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a large truck

indicators.note: something that stops a gap fills it, so this word sits inside the other

parts.note: he is the pronoun for that man
roger in radio talk means message received, OK

explanation.surface: A lorry driven by a man called Roger pulls up carrying vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' looks like the driver's name but is radio jargon for message received. A lorry is a British truck.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Terrible man, one appearing later to be conceited

indicators.note: appearing later means turning up further along, so the letter is moved back into the word

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible was a tsar of Russia
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dreadful fellow, arriving late, seems full of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The I at the front of IVAN moves later in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain describes someone with too high an opinion of their own looks or abilities.

clue.text: French course favourite, one that's somewhat sluggish?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a classic dish served in French restaurants
second meaning: a creature akin to a slug, and famously slow

explanation.surface: A popular French dish, and something rather slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sluggish' is a pun: the snail is literally slug-like as well as slow; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is French for snail, eaten with garlic butter as a starter, and snails are slow relatives of slugs.

clue.text: Exploit type in pursuit of money primarily

indicators.note: pursuing something means coming behind it, so this part goes second
primarily means first of all, so just the opening letter is used

parts.note: the initial of money
ilk means type or kind

explanation.surface: Taking advantage is the sort of thing done mainly for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk someone or something is to exploit it, drawing out every possible advantage.

clue.text: Paper animal, misshapen

indicators.note: misshapen means bent out of its proper form, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deformed creature appears in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is a strong brown paper used for envelopes and folders, first made from Manila hemp.

clue.text: Bloated corporation growing without need for credit

parts.note: corporation is old humorous slang for a pot belly, a tum

indicators.note: doing without something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: crescent as an adjective means growing or increasing, like the waxing moon
CR is the abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: An overblown firm keeps expanding without having to borrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but it is a jocular old word for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumescent means swollen or puffed up, the same as bloated.

clue.text: Head hit planter keeling over

definitions.note: a topknot is hair worn on the head, so this is loose

indicators.note: keeling over means toppling, so in a down clue the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: tonk is British slang for hitting hard, especially in cricket
a pot is a planter for growing plants

explanation.surface: Someone struck on the head by a flowerpot falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is the definition, standing for the tuft of hair worn on top of it; the surface makes it the place struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a knot or tuft of hair, or a crest, on the top of the head.

clue.text: Inventor adapted one's idea, each conceded

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit, so the letters are rearranged
what is conceded is given up, so those letters are surrendered from the rest

parts.note: taken as written
EA is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: An inventor modified his concept, and each one admitted defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Oddball comedian, short of energy travelling around

indicators.note: an oddball is eccentric and peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order
short of means lacking, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An eccentric stand-up, low on energy, is touring the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddball' looks like a description of the comedian; it signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic describes people who roam from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: Express mirth as cost of drug increased

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine; its cost is the price of crack
a price that has increased is up

explanation.surface: Someone laughs on hearing that drug prices have risen.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'cost of crack is up' as a news item.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is an informal idiom for bursting out laughing.

clue.text: Best Sixties rock band

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the finest part of something
second meaning: the British trio of Clapton, Bruce and Baker

explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' reads as praise for the band; it is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its elite, and Cream was a 1960s supergroup trio.

clue.text: Norwegian ready to cycle a single kilometre, right?

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round in a loop, so the end letters are brought to the front

parts.note: a single is one
K is short for kilometre
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Norwegian set to ride a bike for just one kilometre asks for confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE K R cycles to KRONE. 'Ready' is British slang for cash, so 'Norwegian ready' is Norway's money.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the currency of Norway, and ready is informal for money.

clue.text: German left golf course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the German word for left
second meaning: a seaside golf course on sandy ground

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a German leaving the course; 'left' is the opposite of right.
explanation.definitionFit: Links is German for left-hand, and in English means a coastal golf course on dunes.

clue.text: Nothing wrong about claiming retired cleric is lush

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the outer letters go round the others

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
about here means turned around and jumbled, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric
taken as written

explanation.surface: There's no harm in saying a retired vicar is a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like slang for a drunkard, which fits the cleric; here it means rampant with growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush vegetation is thick and abundant, which describes a garden left overgrown.

clue.text: Broken object traps tailless insect

indicators.note: trapping something means enclosing it, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: an object is an aim or purpose, an intent

indicators.note: tailless means without its end, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a termite is a wood-eating insect

explanation.surface: A smashed item has caught a bug without its rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a thing; it means purpose here.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermittent means stopping and starting at intervals, broken rather than continuous.
